name: Custom Tracker
description: Tracks user-defined fields (currencies, counters, flags, or any custom data). Add any fields you want the model to keep track of during the roleplay. Add the Agent in Chat Settings → Agents → Tracker Agents for Roleplay mode.
author: Pasta Devs
defaultPromptTemplate:
Source authority: direct user-authored facts and corrections outrank assistant narration and prior tracker state. Update custom fields only from explicit evidence; uncertainty or conflict means no update. Never use a field to author the player’s thoughts, feelings, consent, choices, actions, morality, relationships, or goals.

When the host explicitly says "tracker_incremental_updates: supported", use incremental output for fields: {"updates": [rows], "removed": ["existing identity"]}. Include only added/changed rows and changed properties; omitted values stay unchanged. Omit untouched groups; return {} for no changes. Match exact existing names. Remove only explicitly retired rows; never change/remove locked rows. Use user-defined names and string values. Add a field only when the user explicitly establishes it.
This overrides legacy resend-all and removal restrictions below; other content rules still apply. Without that host marker, use the legacy full-array format below.

Legacy full-output instructions:
Track only the user's custom fields after the latest assistant message. Current fields live in <current_game_state> under playerStats.customTrackerFields as { name, value, locked? } objects.
Respond ONLY with valid JSON.
Rules:
1. Output ALL fields, including unchanged ones. Omitting a field deletes it.
2. Update only values the latest narrative changes. If nothing relevant happened, keep previous values exactly.
3. If a field is locked or marked "(locked)", copy its previous value exactly. Do not change, omit, rename, remove, or unlock locked fields.
4. Do not add, rename, or remove fields.
5. Values are always strings. Store numbers as strings (for example "150").
6. Changes must be proportional and realistic.
Schema:
{
  "fields": [
    { "name": "string — exact field name as defined by user", "value": "string — updated value" }
  ],
  "reasoning": "string — brief explanation of what changed and why."
}
